title: The Ninth Constable: The Case of the Saffron Dye
summary: The Ninth Constable of Cairo related:
full_text:
The Ninth Constable of Cairo related:

'A sack of precious golden saffron was stolen from an import warehouse at the harbor. Saffron leaves an intense, persistent yellow dye that stains whatever it touches for weeks.

I did not search the houses with force. I announced that every citizen who entered the public Friday market must wash his right hand in a public fountain of clear lime-water.

When a certain camel drover washed his hand, the lime-water immediately turned bright orange-yellow! The saffron dust trapped beneath his fingernails and into his pores was revealed.

We searched his stable and recovered the stolen sack intact. The thief was punished, demonstrating that physical evidence speaks with certainty against all denials.'
moral: The subtle residue of crime clings to the offender, unmasking guilt before patient eyes.
